newsitem.title: UK: Big players kick off London gas futures trade.
newsitem.headline: Big players kick off London gas futures trade.

text.p: Trade in Britain's first natural gas futures contract kicked off on Friday with some of the UK's leading gas traders jostling to make their mark on the launch.
The International Petroleum Exchange (IPE) contract opened with a flurry of deals at the 1000 GMT start, and each of the 12 forward months had traded by the close of the morning session at 1200 GMT.
"We had several trades executed immediately at the 1000 am opening of the market," said Louise Kitchen, director of gas trading at U.S. gas giant Enron Capital and Trade Resources.
Kitchen said Enron believed it had executed the first trade and had opened positions across all months to February 1998.
"Our reaction to the first morning is that we're quite pleased it all worked and we were able to transact successfully", she said.
The IPE said it was satisfied with business on the infant contract's first session.
"I'm pleasantly encouraged with the activity we've seen. It's nice to see all months have traded all the way out," said Richard Ward, the IPE's business development director.

As expected, the market opened closely in line with the UK spot market. The first trade in March was done at 14.900 pence a therm, with the market then tracking lower to a session close of 14.200 pence. Both April and May also saw the lowest trades of the session just before the close.
But dealers said that the market was more interested in the way the contract was working than with the price.
A total of 220 lots, representing 220,000 therms a day, were traded, spread evenly across all periods although July and August saw only one minimum-sized lot traded in each month.

"We're pleasantly surprised by how it's all gone in terms of systems," said a trader with Britain's biggest gas trader Accord Energy, part of British Gas plc. "There have been no hiccups with quote vendors and no technical problems."
Accord had traded "small bits and pieces" on both side of the market with a view to stimulating trade, he said. "Basically we're optimistic for the future."
Enron's Kitchen said there had been some keen interest in the opening five minutes, although trade was thin for much of the rest of the session.
But she said that greater depth appeared as the morning wore on, with more bids and offers seen, even though they were still far apart in many periods.
The contract will reopen at 1400 GMT for a second two-hour session.
